NONE: › also 'd past simple and past participle of
have , also used with the past participle of other verbs to form the past perfect
› (of a machine, etc.) to be in such a bad condition that it is not useful or (of a person, team, etc.) to be doing so badly that they are certain to fail
（機器等）失去效用的，壞的；（人、團體等）肯定失敗的
› to be tricked and given less than you agreed or paid for
受騙，上當

example: I think this computer's had it.
Liverpool have had it for this season.
利物浦隊本賽季是輸定了。

NONE: › used to suggest an action or to show that it is necessary
最好

example: You had best tell her (= it would be wise if you told her) that you won't be able to come to her party.
你最好告訴她，你不能參加她的派對。
We'd best be going now (= we should go now).

NONE: › If you had better/best do something, you should do it or it would be good to do it.
應該，最好

example: I'd better leave a note so they'll know I'll be late.
我最好留張紙條，這樣他們就知道我會晚點到。

NONE: › If someone had it coming, something bad happened to them that was deserved.
是…應得的，活該

example: He's been fired but, with all that time he took off, he had it coming really.
他被解僱了，不過他休假那麼久了，這也真是活該。
